Ensures product/software engineering and AI capabilities align with desired client outcomes.

Delivery Management
Engages in billable client delivery roles, ensuring high-quality outcomes in product engineering and AI capabilities .
Oversees delivery across multiple client accounts and large-scale engineering teams.

Go to Market Approach
Ignites awareness and demand for Product Engineering offerings through proactive sales campaigns, RFIs, RFPs, workshops, and prototypes .
Builds and sustains relationships across target and active client portfolios in your market.
Creates demand by proactively seeking speaking opportunities within the geographic Market as a Capability SME and thought leader at external conferences and events.

Business Development and Sales
Partners with client and sales leaders to identify technology-led opportunities, acting as the Solution Lead or Subject Matter Expert during pursuits.
Participates in multi-capability solutioning and outcome-based selling motions with other Go To market leaders.
Collaborates on growth projections, driving revenue performance against forecasts and identify capability health challenges, aligning corrective actions as needed.
Own the portfolio of sales and revenue of the Software Engineering capability in this market.

Resource Pipeline
Participates in hiring, staffing, and workforce planning rhythms for market and or capability teams.

People Development
Leads and develops teams through direct and indirect reporting relationships to scale go-to-market impact.
Provides performance feedback on Capability team members supporting pursuits and delivery.

What You’ll Bring
You possess deep technology delivery and leadership experience, with a passion for building teams and client partnerships. You are skilled as both a strategic leader and hands-on practitioner, with expertise in product engineering, AI-accelerated engineering, and large-scale delivery models. Your leadership is inspirational and proactive, with a strong emphasis on collaboration, growth, and market-focused strategic thinking.
Core Expertise:
Product Engineering: Extensive experience leading cross-discipline teams (Agile, Software Engineering, Quality Engineering, DevOps, and UX).
Engineering Excellence: Experience establishing modern engineering practices such as CI/CD, test automation, code quality standards, and developer experience improvements across large teams.
Application Architecture and Modernization: Experience leading the design of scalable application architectures, APIs, and microservices, and modernizing legacy applications and platforms.
Digital Product Delivery: Experience guiding digital products from discovery through prototype, launch, and scale, using sound product and engineering trade-offs.
Accelerated Engineering with AI: Deep understanding of how Generative AI is evolving the SDLC and maturing technology organizations.
Team-Based Delivery at Scale: Experience delivering engineering projects using scale teaming models, including Nearshore and Offshore partners.
Product Mindset: Ability to work with customers to shape product strategy, roadmaps, and outcome-based results.
Book of Business Leadership: Experience running a book of business for software engineering, including business planning, revenue forecasting, pipeline management, sales operations, contract negotiation, and escalation management.

Multi-Account Management: Experience managing multiple client accounts with large-scale engineering teams, including executive relationships, delivery oversight, and client escalations.

Leadership Attributes:
Inspirational Leadership: Forward-looking strategic thinking connected to market needs.
Proactive GTM Mentality: A builder of relationships and pipeline who does not wait for leads to be handed to them.
Collaboration: Strong ability to collaborate across different teams and global organizations.
Grow Mindset: Acts as an external speaker at events and speaks to customer CXOs as a peer with credibility and confidence.

About Us
Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. From strategy through delivery, our agile teams across 52 offices in 12 countries partner with clients to co-create powerful customer experiences, modern ways of working, and meaningful impact. 
What sets us apart? We believe work should be challenging and fulfilling, not perfect, but possible. That’s why we prioritize purpose, flexibility, connection, and recognition, so our people can thrive and love what they do, most days. 

Compensation and Benefits
Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, parental leave, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and short/long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses, as well as discounted home, auto, and pet insurance.

Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. For this role, we are hiring at the following levels and targeted base pay salary ranges:  The targeted base salary pay range for Director is $240,000 to $260,000 and the target base salary range for Senior Director is $260,000-$290,000.   In addition, individuals may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus .  Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time.    

We are committed to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. If you have questions or concerns about the pay range or other compensation information in this posting, please contact us at:  peopleone@slalom.com . Please note, this recipient is not able to support recruitment inquiries beyond this purpose.

EEO and Accommodations
Slalom is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to attracting, developing and retaining highly qualified talent who empower our innovative teams through unique perspectives and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. Slalom will also consider qualified applications with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. Slalom welcomes and encourages applications from individuals with disabilities. Reasonable accommodations are available for candidates during all aspects of the selection process. Please advise the talent acquisition team or contact  accomodationrequest@slalom.com  if you require accommodations during the interview process.

new_jobs.description:
About Alaffia & Our Mission

Every year, U.S. health plans lose billions to improper payments and administrative waste. That wasted spending ultimately trickles down across the healthcare ecosystem, driving up costs for plans, providers, and patients alike. We’re here to change that paradigm.

Alaffia is a new kind of claims operations partner for health plans. Using expert clinicians and transparent AI, we deliver deeper insights, smarter automation, and consistently better outcomes across the entire lifecycle of claims. With Alaffia, health plans can cut wasted spending more effectively than ever — and provide their members the most affordable care.

We’re a high-growth, venture-backed Series B healthtech startup based in NYC and are actively scaling our company. Join us in helping to build a healthcare system that works better for everyone.

*This position requires current authorization to work in the United States. Unfortunately, we are not in a position to sponsor work visas at this time.

About the Role & What You’ll Be Doing

Alaffia Health is a healthcare AI startup revolutionizing medical billing and data automation. Our AI-driven platform leverages state-of-the-art generative AI and machine learning technologies to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and compliance in medical billing and auditing
As we scale, we’re looking for an AI Engineer to build the intelligence behind Alaffia’s AI agents. Our agentic systems are already in production reviewing real claims. As our customers’ needs grow more complex, we need someone to make our agents smarter, more accurate, and better grounded in the policies, contracts, and clinical evidence they reason over.
This is a model-focused role spanning four areas. You’ll design and build the agents themselves, including their planning, tool use, and multi-step reasoning across claims and medical records. You’ll develop and fine-tune the LLMs that power them on domain-specific healthcare data. You’ll build the RAG systems that keep their outputs accurate and traceable to source documents. And you’ll apply reinforcement learning techniques such as RLHF and DPO, turning feedback from our clinical auditors into measurable improvements in agent performance.
This role is for you if you like working at the frontier of applied LLM research and seeing your work land in production. You’ll take ideas from early experiments through to models that make real decisions on real claims, and you’ll have a direct hand in shaping how a Series B healthtech builds, trains, and improves its AI. You’ll work closely with our AI engineers, MLOps team, and clinical subject-matter experts.

Your Responsibilities

AI Agent Development:
Design and build single- and multi-agent systems for claim review. This includes planning, tool use, memory, and multi-step reasoning across claims data, medical records, and coding guidelines.
RAG Development:
Build and optimize retrieval-augmented generation pipelines over policies, contracts, clinical guidelines, and medical records. This covers chunking strategies, embeddings, hybrid search, re-ranking, and grounding and citation of outputs.
LLM Development & Fine-Tuning:
Fine-tune open-source and proprietary LLMs (e.g., SFT, LoRA/QLoRA, instruction tuning) on domain-specific healthcare and claims data. Manage dataset curation, training runs, and model versioning.
Reinforcement Learning:
Develop RL-based training and alignment methods (e.g., RLHF, DPO, reward modeling) that use human-in-the-loop feedback from clinical auditors. Use them to improve agent accuracy, reasoning, and decision quality.
Evaluation & Experimentation:
Define evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and metrics for agents, fine-tuned models, and RAG systems. These include hallucination, faithfulness, retrieval quality, and task-level accuracy. Run and track experiments rigorously.
Production Integration (in collaboration with the Software and DevOps teams):
Take models and agents from prototype to production, optimizing for latency, cost, and reliability at scale.
Compliance & Safety:
Ensure models and agents handle PHI securely and comply with HIPAA. Build guardrails that keep outputs accurate, explainable, and auditable.

What We’re Looking For

3+ years of experience in applied ML or AI engineering, ideally with experience developing agentic systems, fine-tuning LLMs, and building RAG pipelines in production.
Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in Python.
Highly experienced in developing AI agents
and agentic workflows, including tool calling, orchestration, and multi-step reasoning
Hands-on experience with LLM fine-tuning
(SFT, PEFT/LoRA) and training pipelines using frameworks such as PyTorch and Hugging Face
Proven experience building production RAG systems
, including vector databases, embedding models, and retrieval optimization
Practical experience applying reinforcement learning
to LLMs (e.g., RLHF, DPO, PPO, reward modeling)
Strong understanding of LLM evaluation methodologies and experiment tracking

Nice to have
Experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or similar
Familiarity with LLM provider APIs and self-hosted model serving (e.g., vLLM, TGI)
Experience with distributed training and GPU infrastructure
Working knowledge of AI tooling
such as MLFlow, LangFuse, and Weights & Biases
Experience with healthcare data (claims, EHRs, medical coding such as ICD-10/CPT) or other regulated domains

Our Culture

Alaffia was born out of our founders’ personal connection to the inefficiency of the U.S. healthcare system. We are deeply mission-driven, with an abiding belief that technology can help create a better future for everyone — and we’re looking for others who share our passion for change to join the team.

What Else Do You Get Working With Us?

Competitive Compensation

Flexible, paid vacation policy
Work in a flat organizational structure — direct access to Leadership

PreScalar is building the most advanced automated test platform, solving problems from early R&D all the way to full-scale factory solutions. We specialize in functional testing of hardware subsystems at production volume, for products that combine electronics, firmware, and software.
Our customers span autonomous vehicles, robotics, defense, and medical systems.

About the Role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you make PreScalar work on a customer’s floor, owning deployments from the first technical conversation to a test station running in production.
You’ll work from our San Francisco shop and alongside customers that include some of the leading hardware companies in the world, scoping test coverage one week and debugging a fixture on a production line the next. The pace is fast, so you’ll need to be dynamic and steady under pressure. Your field learnings shape what we build. You’re as comfortable with a scope, a soldering iron, and a Python script as you are leading a customer meeting.

What You’ll Do

Lead customer deployments of PreScalar test systems, including fixtures, HIL benches, and automated test stations, from kickoff through production sign-off.
Work with customer hardware, firmware, and manufacturing engineers to understand their products and turn requirements into test plans and coverage.
Bring up and integrate test hardware on site: wiring, instrumentation, power, CAN/Ethernet/serial interfaces, and DUT connections.
Write and maintain test software and automation in Python, and integrate with customer firmware, tooling, and data systems.
Diagnose failures across the stack, whether the root cause is the device, the fixture, the firmware, or the test code.
Train customer operators and technicians, and write the documentation and user guides that keep stations running after you leave.
Feed field learnings back to product and engineering so every deployment makes the platform better.
Support pre-sales scoping and technical proposals alongside the founders.

What We’re Looking For

5+ years of hands-on engineering in robotics, autonomous vehicles, embedded systems, test engineering, or a similar hardware-heavy field.
A degree in electrical, mechanical, computer, or systems engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong Python skills for automation, data handling, and test scripting.
Solid electronics fundamentals: reading schematics, using oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and logic analyzers.
Experience with at least one common hardware interface, such as CAN, Ethernet, UART, SPI, or I2C.
A track record of debugging complex systems where hardware, firmware, and software all interact.
Clear communication with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders, and the judgment to own a customer relationship.
Willingness to travel to customer sites, typically 15–25% of the time.

Nice to Have

Experience building or running hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) benches or production test stations.
Background in automotive, AV, robotics, defense, or medical device manufacturing environments.
Familiarity with ROS/ROS 2, Linux systems administration, or embedded C/C++.
Experience with test frameworks and data tooling (pytest, OpenHTF, or similar), plus dashboards and results databases.
Fixture design exposure: CAD, harnessing, pogo-pin or bed-of-nails fixtures.
Prior customer-facing work as a field, applications, solutions, or forward deployed engineer.

Real ownership on a small team, with a direct line to the founders.
Exposure to a wide range of frontier companies across Silicon Valley, across autonomous vehicles, robotics, defense, and medical systems.
Work on hardware that ships: autonomous vehicles, robotics, defense, and medical systems.

new_jobs.description:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

About The Role

Socure is the leading provider of digital identity verification and fraud prevention solutions, leveraging AI and machine learning to power the most accurate identity trust decisions. Our mission is to eliminate identity fraud and ensure online trust across industries.

We are seeking a Senior Data Scientist
to join our Digital Intelligence
team. In this role, you will drive the development of machine learning features and models that leverage device, network, and behavioral data to power fraud prevention and identity verification. You’ll work with rich, high-volume data from browser, mobile, and API traffic to surface meaningful insights and scalable risk signals. This is a great opportunity to own impactful projects, collaborate cross-functionally, and deepen your expertise in applied ML for device and behavioral intelligence.

What You'll Do

Design and deploy advanced machine learning systems for device identification, anomaly detection, and fraud prevention—balancing precision, recall, and real-world adversarial dynamics.
Contribute to the development of scalable data pipelines and production ML workflows using structured and unstructured telemetry (e.g., browser, mobile, session data).
Investigate high-complexity signals (e.g., emulator use, spoofing, low-entropy fingerprints), applying advanced statistical methods and domain knowledge to detect fraud and abuse.
Translate ambiguous business problems into modeling approaches, using a combination of supervised, unsupervised, and heuristic techniques.
Partner with engineering, product, and risk teams to contribute to data architecture decisions, signal collection, and planning.
Drive experimental design, A/B testing frameworks, and robust validation techniques to ensure model generalizability and long-term trust.
Contribute to team standards for ML explainability, risk evaluation, and feature logging.
Document methodologies and communicate results effectively through dashboards, presentations, and reports for both technical and executive audiences.
Mentor junior data scientists and participate in cross-functional working groups.

What You Bring

Master’s degree (or equivalent practical experience) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related quantitative field.
6+ years of experience in data science or applied machine learning, including experience working in production environments.
Excellent SQL skills and extensive experience with large-scale databases and data modeling.
Proven track record of deploying and maintaining ML models in live systems, ideally involving streaming or near-real-time data.
Proficiency in Python and distributed computing tools (e.g., Spark, PySpark).
Hands-on experience with ML frameworks such as scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, or similar.
Excellent communication skills—able to explain complex technical results to non-technical stakeholders and senior leadership.
Experience designing and interpreting experiments, working with real-world noisy datasets, and applying sound validation techniques to assess model robustness.
Demonstrated ability to break down ambiguous problems, apply analytical rigor, and uncover meaningful insights that influence product or risk strategies.
Strong judgment across data quality, model selection, and business impact tradeoffs.
Collaborative mindset and experience working cross-functionally with product, engineering, and analytics teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in fraud detection, behavioral biometrics, anomaly detection, or adversarial modeling.
Experience with high-cardinality feature engineering techniques (e.g., frequency/target encoding, embeddings).
Familiarity with privacy-preserving or robust ML techniques.
Knowledge of browser/mobile fingerprinting, VPN/proxy detection, or telemetry signal processing.

What You’ll Gain

Hands-on experience with real-world data science challenges in a high-impact industry.
A collaborative and inclusive work environment that fosters learning and growth.
Opportunities to grow into staff-level or technical leadership roles over time.

new_jobs.description:

At Slalom, we co-create modern technology and software products with clients who are ready to accelerate their digital product development. We imagine how things can be made better, then set out to realize what’s possible — driving innovation with quality, resilience, and purpose. This includes architecting multi-agent systems, LLM-powered autonomous workflows, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and enterprise-grade AI governance frameworks using cutting-edge orchestration frameworks, tool-use protocols, and cloud-native AI services. You’ll help clients move from isolated proofs of concept to secure, scalable, observable systems that create real business value, while helping craft projects in their initial phases and delivering them with a team. Provide thought leadership on AI/ML, Generative AI, and Agentic AI internally and with clients, while contributing to a culture of collaboration, learning, and curiosity
Design end-to-end agentic AI architectures including planning loops, memory management, tool integration, and agent coordination patterns
Architect multi-agent orchestration systems using frameworks such asStrands Agents SDK,OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Lang Graph or similar for autonomous reasoning, decision-making, and task execution

Build advanced retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems including vector databases, embedding strategies, chunking optimization, hybrid search, re-ranking, and multi-source data synthesis

Travel may be required on a limited basis dependent on your client engagement or internal meetings/events.

What You’ll Bring

5+ years of software engineering experience building and deploying production systems; experience with machine learning, applied AI, or intelligent software systems is a plus, with 2+ years focused on generative AI, LLMs, or agentic AI systems
Hands-on experience designing or building multi-agent systems including agent orchestration, tool integration, and autonomous decision-making workflows
Proficiency with at least one agentic AI or workflow framework such as Lang Graph, Strands, AutoGen, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, or similar
Experience with RAG architectures including vector databases, embeddings, and retrieval optimization, and context management techniques such as chunking, summarization, and memory handling
Experience developing production-ready solutions on at least one major cloud AI platform, such as AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry/OpenAI Service, GCP Vertex AI/Gemini, or Databricks; experience operating and maintaining production environments is a plus
Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Kiro, or similar IDE-based coding agents, including effective use for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and developer workflow acceleration
Strong Python development skills; experience withFastAPI, Flask, or equivalent API frameworks
Experience building ML or AI systems end to end, including data access, feature or retrieval flows, APIs, testing, deployment, and production support
Familiarity with evaluation frameworks, tracing, observability, model behavior analysis, and regression testing for GenAI systems
Understanding of prompt engineering, LLM fine-tuning, chain-of-thought reasoning, and structured output techniques
Recognized as an authority on at least one technical domain (e.g., Agentic Systems, RAG, Multi-Agent Orchestration) with generalist familiarity across AI/ML techniques
Ability to work across new domains and unfamiliar data structures and lead exploratory analysis when requirements are not fully defined
Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to lead highly technical presentations
Familiarity with Agile project delivery
(Preferred) Experience with Model Context Protocol (MCP) server development and integration
(Preferred) Experience with MLOps/LLMOps pipelines, CI/CD for ML, and model monitoring/observability

About Us

Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. From strategy through delivery, our agile teams across 52 offices in 12 countries partner with clients to co-create powerful customer experiences, modern ways of working, and meaningful impact. Compensation and Benefits 

Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, parental leave, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and short/long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses, as well as discounted home, auto, and pet insurance.

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Located in the nation’s capital, the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) is the chief legal office of the District of Columbia. OAG enforces the laws of the District, defends, and provides legal advice to the District’s government agencies and protects the interests of the District’s residents. This position is located within the Immediate Office.

The Immediate Office sets the direction for the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). It is responsible for establishing the policy priorities that the organization pursues and ensuring that the OAG consistently provides high-quality legal services to the District agencies the OAG supports.

The position will place particular emphasis on juvenile and criminal justice: using agency data to evaluate the effectiveness of the office’s criminal and juvenile justice work; looking at data from the juvenile justice, abuse and neglect, and child support systems to inform the work the office does with vulnerable youth; and making appropriate aggregate public safety data available to the public in line with open and transparent government. The Data Scientist will support OAG's efforts to use data and analytics to evaluate programs, improve operations, enhance transparency, and inform policy and strategic decision-making. The incumbent will work collaboratively with attorneys, investigators, analysts, and agency leadership to develop data-driven insights and analytical products.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Data Scientist will be responsible for developing computational algorithms and statistical methods to find patterns and relationships in multiple database sources. new_jobs.description:
Build the deterministic AI execution layer for enterprise operations

> Our Thesis:
While consumer AI tools and coding assistants (like Claude Code) focus on unconstrained, single-user tasks, mission-critical enterprise operations require a fundamentally different architecture. Enterprise adoption cannot rely on free-roaming personal agents. It demands deterministic execution engines, robust operational guardrails, automated verification loops, and bulletproof process orchestration.

Enterprise software integrations are still painfully fragile: workflows break silently, APIs fail unpredictably, systems drift out of sync, and teams waste countless hours maintaining infrastructure never built for real-time operations at scale.

Our platform powers operations for supply chains, logistics, healthcare, financial operations, e-commerce, and enterprise sales. When our systems run, AI agents execute business processes deterministically: orders move, invoices sync, warehouses operate, contracts renew, revenue gets recognized, and critical workflows execute in real time.

What You Will Work On in Your First 90 Days

Deterministic Execution Engines: Build production-grade AI agents designed for structured process execution rather than open-ended chat loops.
Guardrails & Evaluation Suites: Implement programmatic guardrails, schema enforcement, human-in-the-loop fallback triggers

This Role IS for You If

You understand why enterprise AI requires strict guardrails, transactional guarantees, and deterministic process execution over unconstrained agents.
You are a systems-minded full-stack engineer who loves tackling difficult backend, distributed queue, and non-deterministic agent problems.
You think like a product owner, take end-to-end ownership, and thrive in fast-moving startup environments.

This Role IS NOT for You If

You think building enterprise AI is just writing prompts or making simple calls to OpenAI/Anthropic APIs.
You dislike operational complexity or debugging non-deterministic failure modes and state drift.
You require long, slow timelines or highly structured corporate environments.

Tech Stack & Tooling

Languages & Frameworks:
Python, React, Postgres

⚠️ Apply By Answering ⚠️

What excites you about building guardrailed, process-executing AI execution engines over open-ended chat assistants? (2–3 sentences max)
What is the most technically complex agent workflow, guardrail system, or real-time distributed pipeline you've built? Highlight how you handled state, failure modes, or verification loops.

Your role will involve researching, building, and implementing scalable AI, machine learning, generative AI, and agentic systems on Databricks that learn, reason, and generate outputs tailored to diverse business environments. Your Key Responsibilities

You will help our clients navigate the complex world of modern data science, analytics, and software engineering. We'll look to you to provide guidance and perform technical development tasks to ensure AI solutions are responsibly engineered, evaluated, deployed, and maintained to support the ongoing business needs of our clients.

You will be joining a dynamic and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers who love to tackle the most challenging computational problems for our clients. We love to think creatively, build applications efficiently, and collaborate in both the ideation of solutions and the pursuit of new opportunities. Many on our team have advanced academic degrees or equivalent experience in industry.

This position may have travel requirements as needed to engage with external clients regularly

This role will work to deliver tech at speed, innovate at scale and put humans at the center. Provide technical guidance and share knowledge with team members with diverse skills and backgrounds. Consistently deliver quality client services focusing on more complex, judgmental and/or specialized issues surrounding emerging technology. Demonstrate technical capabilities and professional knowledge. Learn about EY and its service lines and actively assess and present ways to apply knowledge and services.

Translating AI strategy into a implementable Model Engineering activities that aligns with the client’s goals, mission and vision

Implementing product-centric AI solutions on Databricks, from discovery and roadmap definition through iterative delivery, adoption, and continuous improvement, with measurable business and user outcomes
Working across design, build, deploy, and operate phases to deliver production-grade data and AI pipelines, including governed business ontologies and semantic models on Databricks, so solutions remain reliable, reusable, and aligned with client business processes
Applying a product-centric development approach to data and AI solutions by defining user outcomes, prioritizing reusable capabilities, managing roadmaps and backlogs, incorporating user feedback, measuring adoption and business value, and continuously improving products after launch
Staying abreast of AI technology trends and provide directional guidance and recommendations around AIOps, MLOps, and AgentOps tools and solutions on Databricks that fit their needs and integrate with their existing ecosystem
Applying combined business and technical knowledge to develop and execute ModelOps target architecture on Databricks that enables implementation and monitoring of AI at scale, with tools like Unity Catalog and Model Serving
Collaborating with Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Cloud Engineers, and Platform Engineers, DevOps to implement and sustain solutions in the Databricks platform
Understanding clients’ overall data, AI and technology landscape and business priorities and success measures

Working on large-scale client engagements. Fostering relationships with client personnel at appropriate levels. Consistently delivering quality client services. Driving high-quality work products within expected timeframes and on budget
Collaborating, influencing and building consensus through constructive relationships and effective listening

Databricks Certification with a minimum of 1 professional and 1 associate certification that includes a combination of Data Engineer Associate or Professional, Machine Learning Associate or Professional, Generative AI Engineer Associate, and/or Context Engineering Associate
Strong skills in Python, PySpark, and/or Scala

Experience with natural language processing and deep learning
Extensive experience in DevOps tools (Git, Azure DevOps) and AI-driven SDLC for developing, deploying, and scaling analytical solutions on Databricks, for example with Databricks Git folders, Declarative Automation Bundles, and the Databricks CLI and SDKs
Experience with MLOps, LLMOps, and AgentOps and ML workflows on Databricks, including data ingestion, transformation, and evaluation, for example with MLflow, Models in Unity Catalog, and Model Serving
Experience with model retraining and feedback loop methodologies on Databricks, for example with Lakeflow Jobs and Databricks Feature Store
Experience evaluating and operating models and AI solutions on Databricks, including observability, monitoring, reporting, MLflow evaluation and tracing, and data quality monitoring.
Understanding of data structures, Responsible AI practices, and data modelling, and software engineering best practices

Excellent communication skills for conveying findings and recommendations, with willingness to travel as needed for client engagements.

Master's degree Computer Science, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, or another quantitative field
Databricks Solution Architect Champion Badge preferred
Experience in hybrid collaboration and emotional agility

A deep understanding of and ability to teach concepts, tools, features, functions, and benefits of different approaches to apply them

Experience with image processing techniques and/or speech and audio processing and analysis

We seek individuals who are not only technically proficient but also possess the qualities of a top performer. Your ability to collaborate effectively and communicate with clarity will set you apart as a leader in our team.

new_jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, ML API – AI Inference
new_jobs.description:
Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services.

This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation.

Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference.

About The Role

Cerebras is building a new generation of disaggregated AI inference systems that combine GPU-accelerated prefill with ultra-fast decode on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine.

We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to build and evolve the ML API layer that makes this heterogeneous serving system accessible, reliable, and easy to use. You will own significant features and components across our inference APIs, model integration layer, and request-routing services, delivering a consistent experience across models and accelerator backends.

This role sits at the intersection of machine learning systems, API design, model serving, and distributed systems. You will translate evolving model capabilities and customer requirements into clear designs, lead implementation across multiple components, and carry features through validation, rollout, and production operation. Your work will help ensure that streaming, sampling, tool use, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and model configuration behave correctly and consistently.

You will work closely with model enablement, compiler, runtime, cloud infrastructure, product, and customer-facing teams, as well as customers directly. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with opportunities to lead small project teams, mentor engineers, and improve the quality and reliability of production inference software.

Responsibilities

Own features end to end. Design, implement, test, and operate features for chat completions, text generation, streaming, model configuration, tool calling, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and emerging inference capabilities.
Lead multi-component delivery. Write clear design documents, evaluate technical tradeoffs, break projects into deliverable milestones, and coordinate implementation with a small group of engineers and partner teams.
Deliver consistent API behavior. Implement clear request and response semantics across GPU prefill, Cerebras decode, and other inference backends. Maintain compatibility with widely adopted inference interfaces and evolve owned APIs through validation, versioning, and deprecation best practices.
Enable new models and capabilities. Integrate foundation models, tokenizers, chat templates, generation configuration, sampling methods, and model-specific features into the serving platform.
Integrate serving components. Extend inference services and their integration with frameworks and runtimes such as vLLM, PyTorch, Hugging Face libraries, LLGuidance, and Cerebras runtime components.
Support disaggregated inference. Implement routing, state-transfer integration, error handling, retries, cancellation, and request lifecycle management to coordinate GPU prefill with Cerebras decode.
Deliver measurable performance improvements. Diagnose bottlenecks and improve time to first token, streaming latency, throughput, and resource efficiency through changes to tokenization, serialization, batching, scheduling, and communication.
Own correctness and release quality. Build conformance tests, model-validation suites, numerical comparisons, integration tests, and performance benchmarks that catch regressions in owned features and support safe releases.
Strengthen production reliability. Improve service metrics, tracing, logging, alerts, and diagnostic tools. Investigate production incidents, resolve root causes, and follow through on improvements to resilience and incident response.
Improve customer and developer experience. Partner with product, support, and solutions teams to understand user needs and make practical tradeoffs. Improve configuration, documentation, examples, and debugging workflows.
Raise the engineering quality bar. Provide thoughtful design and code reviews, mentor less-experienced engineers, share domain knowledge, and proactively remove delivery roadblocks.

Minimum Qualifications

5+ years of software engineering experience, including independent ownership of production services, distributed systems, or substantial software components.
Strong programming ability in Python and proficiency in Go, C++, Rust, or another language used to build production services.
Experience designing and delivering features that span multiple components, including documenting designs, evaluating tradeoffs, and coordinating implementation with other engineers.
Experience building and evolving production APIs, with sound practices for validation, error handling, compatibility, and testing. Familiarity with REST, gRPC, or streaming protocols.
Experience integrating software across service, framework, runtime, or infrastructure boundaries.
Experience operating services on Linux using containers, Kubernetes or comparable orchestration systems, and CI/CD.
Ability to diagnose correctness, reliability, and performance issues across distributed components and deliver measurable improvements.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, including experience leading technical delivery for a small project and supporting other engineers through reviews or mentorship.
Ability to turn ambiguous requirements into maintainable software while balancing customer needs, delivery timelines, and operational quality.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building or operating production ML or LLM inference APIs, including OpenAI-compatible interfaces.
Experience extending or contributing to vLLM, SGLang, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Triton, TensorRT-LLM, or another ML systems project.
Understanding of tokenization, chat templates, generation configuration, logits processing, stopping criteria, tool calling, structured generation, or constrained decoding.
Experience with disaggregated prefill/decode architectures, KV-cache transfer, prefix caching, chunked prefill, or inference request scheduling.
Experience building API conformance, model-quality, numerical-comparison, determinism, or performance-regression test systems.
Experience with multi-model or multi-tenant serving, including routing, admission control, quotas, rate limiting, or capacity-aware scheduling.
Experience developing performance-sensitive or highly concurrent services in Go, C++, Rust, or a similar language.
Familiarity with GPU inference, AMD Instinct accelerators, ROCm, CUDA, collective communication, or multi-node model serving.
Familiarity with reduced-precision inference and quantization formats such as BF16, FP8, FP4, INT8, or INT4.
Experience building SDKs, developer tools, configuration systems, or self-service ML workflows, or collaborating directly with customers and open-source communities.

Why Join Cerebras

About

People who are serious about software make their own hardware. At Cerebras, we have built a breakthrough architecture that is unlocking new opportunities for the AI industry. With dozens of model releases and rapid growth, we’ve reached an inflection point in our business. Members of our team tell us there are five main reasons they joined Cerebras:

Build a breakthrough AI platform beyond the constraints of the GPU.
Publish and open source their cutting-edge AI research.
Work on one of the fastest AI supercomputers in the world.
Enjoy job stability with startup vitality.
Our simple, non-corporate work culture that respects individual beliefs.

Find out more about what it's like to work at Cerebras here
!

Apply today and become part of the forefront of groundbreaking advancements in AI!

Cerebras Systems is committed to creating an equal and diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We believe inclusive teams build better products and companies. We try every day to build a work environment that empowers people to do their best work through continuous learning, growth and support of those around them.

We are looking for the best

About Us

42dot is a mobility AI company committed to solving mobility challenges with software and AI. As the Global Software Center of Hyundai Motor Group, 42dot pioneers the future of mobility by advancing the development of software-defined vehicles.

We develop safety-first, user-centric software-defined vehicle technologies that deliver the latest performance through continuous updates like smartphones. By advancing software and AI technology, 42dot envisions a world where everything is connected and moves autonomously through a self-managing urban transportation operating system.

About The Role

Develop driving and physical AI foundation models. Support Aria VLA model development.

Responsibilities

new_jobs.title: Applied Scientist, Context Graph Team
new_jobs.description:
About Skan

Skan automates automation. We capture how work actually happens across an organization and autonomously turn that observation into automation. We are now building toward agentic automation of that work: systems that operate over observed process data and generate Agentic Operating Procedures, structured and auditable playbooks mined from direct observation that allow agents to understand the steps, decisions, branches, and exceptions that define how work is actually performed.

We are a small and passionate team of researchers, engineers, and domain experts working on the next generation of agentic automation: self-discovered AI agents that can understand and operate real enterprise software.

About The Role

Before an agent can reliably operate software on a user's behalf, it needs to understand what should happen next and why: the underlying process, its steps, decision points and governing logic, branches, variations, dependencies, and long-tail edge cases. In practice, this knowledge is rarely represented explicitly. It is distributed across messy event logs, unstructured documents, screen recordings, UI interaction traces, historical executions, and the tacit knowledge of domain experts.

As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will work across teams to develop process-agnostic, scalable learning systems that recover the latent structure, decision logic, and dynamics underlying complex process execution trajectories from sparse, noisy, highly correlated observations spanning substantial behavioral heterogeneity and organizational scale.

You will take heterogeneous data such as action logs, noisy screen traces, semi-structured documents, and variant-heavy workflows, and build systems that recover canonical process structure, meaningful variations, decision rules, dependencies, exceptions, and provenance. These representations are consumed by downstream agentic execution systems and must preserve enough detail for an agent to act correctly while remaining structured, compact, transparent, and auditable.

The same observational data and learned representations also contribute directly to our work on computer-use models for last-mile interaction with enterprise software.

The problems here rarely arrive with clean formulations. You may begin with a branch the system consistently fails to recover, two superficially different execution paths that should collapse into the same process, or an algorithm that works across thousands of traces but fails at millions. Your job is to turn those failures into tractable research problems: identify the right abstraction, formulate hypotheses, design evaluations that isolate the problem, and develop methods that solve it. Depending on the problem, this may draw from process and decision mining, graph algorithms, structured prediction, representation learning, information retrieval, program synthesis, model post-training and distillation, or agentic systems.

We care less about allegiance to a particular technique than about finding the simplest method that reliably recovers the underlying structure and scales.

Responsibilities

Process discovery and representation: Build pipelines that discover, extract, and formalize end-to-end business processes from event logs, UI interaction traces, screen recordings, and unstructured documents.
Develop algorithms for process variant detection, noise removal, and trace consolidation, turning noisy, high-cardinality action sequences into clean canonical representations.
Design representations that preserve the information downstream agents need while collapsing irrelevant execution-level variation.
Study the tradeoff between abstraction and fidelity: determine when superficially different trajectories represent the same underlying behavior and when small differences encode materially different decisions.
Build retrieval and grounding systems that incorporate SOPs, documents, and domain knowledge when process understanding requires evidence beyond execution traces.
Evaluation and reliability: Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks for process discovery and extraction, including LLM-as-Judge pipelines, conformance checking against ground-truth processes, and regression suites that catch subtle degradation.
Develop evaluation methods for settings where there may not be a single canonical ground truth, including behaviorally equivalent process representations.
Enumerate and systematically test exception paths, conditional branches, loops, rare variants, and the failure modes that naive extraction approaches miss.
Make deliberate algorithmic tradeoffs so systems remain tractable across millions of traces and thousands of variants, including choices around data structures, approximation, indexing, and level of abstraction.
Diagnose failures in production and turn recurring failure patterns into new algorithmic or research directions.
Collaboration: Work closely with the computer-use agents team so the representations you produce are expressed at the right level of abstraction, contain the necessary execution context, and are robust enough for downstream autonomous execution.
Work across research, engineering, and product to move promising methods from prototype to production and measure their effect on downstream agent behavior.

Requirements

Ambitious and Hungry: "Far and away the best prize that life offers is the chance to work hard at work worth doing." - Theodore Roosevelt. We screen for comparable experience and strong fundamentals, not exact tool matches. Equivalent technologies are welcome.
Problem Decomposition and Algorithmic Thinking: You can take a loosely defined problem, such as recovering a reliable process from messy action logs, decompose it into tractable sub-problems, reason carefully about edge cases, and arrive at an approach. You are comfortable reasoning from first principles about data structures, graph algorithms, approximation, indexing, and time and space complexity when algorithms must operate over millions of executions.
ML, DL Breadth: Strong working knowledge across representation learning, sequence modeling, clustering, structured prediction, information retrieval, generative modeling, and modern foundation-model adaptation. You have the judgment to recognize when a problem calls for a learned model, an algorithmic solution, an LLM-based system, or some combination of the three.
Cross-Domain Research Translation: You read research from adjacent areas including frontier AI, computer vision, language modelling, process mining, program synthesis, information retrieval, graph learning, and knowledge representation, and can judge whether it applies. You can identify the core idea inside a method, understand the assumptions that make it work, determine whether those assumptions hold in your setting, and adapt the idea into a working prototype.
Research Judgment: You can distinguish a difficult engineering problem from a research problem, design experiments that isolate the important variable, and abandon an elegant approach when the evidence suggests a simpler method works better.
Applied Foundation Model Systems: Hands-on experience building reliable systems with modern language or multimodal models, including retrieval, structured generation, evaluation, grounding, and model adaptation. You understand the failure modes that arise when model outputs are used to recover structured process knowledge from noisy evidence.

This May Include Experience With

Retrieval design, embedding strategies, chunking, re-ranking, and grounding against source evidence.
LLM-as-Judge systems, rubric design, calibration against human labels, and knowing when automated evaluation is insufficient.
Getting hands-on experience with LLMs, RL, RLHF, RLAIF, post-training (SFT), evals, graders, synthetic data, model training and production ML systems.
Faithfulness verification, constrained generation, confidence calibration, and methods for reducing unsupported model outputs.
Guardrails, input and output validation, graceful degradation, and monitoring for drift in production.
Python Proficiency: Strong software engineering in Python, experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, comfort with data processing at scale, and the ability to write clean, tested, production-quality code.
Communication: You can explain an algorithmic tradeoff to both a researcher and a product manager, and you write clear technical and design documents.

Preferred Experience

A strong research track record, demonstrated through publications in top-tier machine learning, artificial intelligence, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, computer vision, or data mining venues.
Experience translating research ideas from published work into production systems with measurable impact.
Process mining: event log analysis, process discovery algorithms, conformance checking, or variant analysis.
Information extraction from documents: NER, relation extraction, table extraction, or structured output generation from unstructured text.
Multimodal data processing: extracting signals from screen recordings, UI screenshots, or interaction traces alongside textual data.
Foundation-model adaptation, including supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, synthetic-data methods, distillation, reinforcement-learning-based post-training, and evaluation of resulting model behavior.

You Might Be a Great Fit If You

Look for the hidden structure inside messy observations before deciding what to build. You are excited by the possibility of discovering how a process actually works without being handed its rules in advance.
Enjoy problems where the right abstraction, model, and formulation are not obvious. You are willing to move between algorithms, learned representations, graph structures, retrieval, and foundation models until the system can explain what it has observed.
Are drawn to the idea of building an end-to-end, process-agnostic machine: one that can observe unfamiliar work, infer its underlying boundaries, steps and decision logic, distinguish meaningful variation from noise, and produce concretized knowledge that gives an agent the full state representation to successfully navigate complex real-world processes.
Read deeply across fields and adapt ideas from process mining, program synthesis, representation learning, graph algorithms, information retrieval, multimodal learning, and agentic systems. You care about the underlying insight more than the category it came from.
Are comfortable moving between theory and reality: papers, hypotheses, experiments, raw traces, screen recordings, production failures, and systems that must work at organizational scale.
Want to work with a small, unusually ambitious team where research judgment and engineering execution are inseparable, and where your ideas can shape the architecture of an entirely new kind of system.

new_jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - AI Audio / Voice Engineer
new_jobs.description:
San Francisco Bay Area · Full-time · 180k-350k · 2-5 years experience

ABOUT NIRVA

Nirva is building the first AI fashion accessory for your mind — a necklace or bracelet that privately listens only to the wearer to enable proactive journaling, emotion tracking, and life coaching. Think Oura Ring for your Mind.
Backed by Lightspeed and South Park Commons, recognized at CES within 90 days of founding, and launching in the U.S. this fall. Co-founders bring backgrounds from Meta Reality Labs (Quest, Ray-Ban glasses) and fashion industry.

THE ROLE

We’re looking for an AI Audio / Voice Engineer to build the audio front door to Nirva’s intelligence layer: the systems that capture only the wearer, reliably, privately, and with as much processing on device as possible. This is the trust foundation for the whole product. If Nirva cannot tell who is speaking, reject everyone else, and do it in noisy real life without draining the battery or sending raw audio where it should not go, nothing built on top of it works. You will own voiceprint, on-device audio, and the technical systems behind our privacy promise, and work directly with the founding team to build them from the ground up.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Voiceprint: build speaker enrollment, voice embeddings, verification and identification so Nirva recognizes the wearer and separates them from bystanders, family, coworkers, and media
Tune and evaluate voiceprint in the real world: false accepts, false rejects, noisy cafes, walking, wind, cars, quiet rooms, illness, and voice drift over time, plus re-enrollment and recovery flows
Anti-spoofing and trust protections: replay and impersonation resistance, liveness signals where relevant, and clear fallbacks when confidence is low
On-device audio: design the on-device pipeline for voice activity detection, segmentation, speaker filtering, audio preprocessing, noise suppression, and streaming to speech recognition, with tight latency, power, thermal, and memory budgets
Decide the on-device vs. cloud split for each audio task and build graceful fallbacks when connectivity, battery, or confidence changes
Trust by design: on-device first processing, bystander exclusion, consent and recording controls, encryption in transit and at rest, data minimization, retention and deletion controls, and user-visible controls that match what the system actually does
Build evals and data pipelines for audio: test sets across people, accents, environments, and devices, failure analysis, and systematic debugging of real user-facing failures
Partner with product, design, and the memory / AI teams so clean, trusted, wearer-only audio becomes transcripts, memories, and experiences users can rely on

Must-haves
2+ years of full-time engineering experience, or a PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, machine learning, speech / audio, or a related field, plus 2 applied internships (industry or applied research) where you shipped or evaluated real systems
Deep, hands-on knowledge of at least one of these, and working knowledge of the other two: 1) voiceprint / speaker verification and identification, 2) on-device audio ML, 3) trust, privacy, and security for audio sensing
Hands-on experience with speech and audio ML in production: speaker embeddings, diarization, VAD, streaming audio, speech-to-text interfaces, audio preprocessing, or speech event detection
Experience running ML on device or at the edge: model quantization, distillation, latency and power optimization, and working within hardware constraints
Strong eval mindset for audio: you can build a test set, measure false accept / false reject and word error tradeoffs, find why a failure happened, and improve the system, not just the demo
Strong product engineering instincts and high ownership: you identify what needs to happen and drive it to shipped quality
Comfortable with ambiguous, human-centered problems where “good” is not easy to measure, and energized by 0-to-1 work, fast iteration, and early-stage startup intensity
Based in San Francisco and able to work in person

Strong signals (nice-to-haves)
Shipped always-on or low-power audio, wearables, hearables, or mobile audio products
Experience with anti-spoofing, voice liveness, or biometric security and its failure modes
iOS audio, Core ML, or embedded / DSP experience
Privacy engineering, on-device personal data systems, or consumer trust and safety for sensing products
Experience spanning audio ML, backend infrastructure, and user-facing surfaces

Collaborating, influencing and building consensus through constructive relationships and effective listening
Solving problems by incorporating data into decision making

Strong skills in Python, PySpark, and/or Scala

Delivered models or agents to production on Databricks, with tracking, evaluation, and monitoring.

Experience with natural language processing and deep learning

Experience with MLOps, LLMOps, and AgentOps and ML workflows on Databricks, including data ingestion, transformation, and evaluation, for example with MLflow, Models in Unity Catalog, and Model Serving
Experience with model retraining and feedback loop methodologies on Databricks, for example with Lakeflow Jobs and Databricks Feature Store
Experience evaluating and operating models and AI solutions on Databricks, including observability, monitoring, reporting, MLflow evaluation and tracing, and data quality monitoring.
Understanding of data structures, Responsible AI practices, and data modelling, and software engineering best practices

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About The Role

Ramp is building a new AI business, and you’ll be one of its first technical sellers. Your job is to turn technically complex AI products into closed revenue.

You’ll sell a growing portfolio spanning AI-powered applications and agents for finance teams, as well as infrastructure that helps companies deploy and manage AI with greater control, security, and cost efficiency. This is a product-focused, quota-carrying technical sales role. You’ll help customers evaluate and purchase Ramp’s AI products, translating complex capabilities into clear business value and guiding opportunities from discovery through close.

This is a high-velocity commercial role, not a traditional pre-sales position where success ends with a great demo. You’ll be accountable for turning technical evaluations into commercial wins from start to finish. You’ll lead discovery, shape deal strategy, build executive-level business cases, deliver tailored demonstrations, navigate technical and commercial objections, and create urgency around a clear path to purchase.

You’ll move comfortably between technical and executive conversations. In one meeting, you may discuss model routing, APIs, integrations, data governance, and security with Engineering and IT teams. In the next, you may help Finance and executive leaders understand the ROI, total cost of ownership, and operational impact of adopting Ramp’s AI products.

You’ll join at a formative moment for Ramp’s AI business. As one of the first dedicated sellers for these products, you’ll help identify the strongest use cases, refine how we position and sell the portfolio, influence the customer experience, and build the playbook the broader team will eventually scale. You’ll own the full customer lifecycle from discovery and evaluation through close, implementation, and adoption, helping customers translate their purchase into a successful deployment. This role combines Ramp’s resources and customer reach with the ownership, speed, and ambiguity of an early-stage team.

What you’ll do

Carry a revenue quota and own the progression of AI product opportunities from initial discovery through purchase, ensuring business value is clear, technical requirements are validated, and obstacles to a decision are resolved.
Lead discovery with business and technical buyers to understand their goals, workflows, challenges, decision criteria, existing systems, and AI strategy.
Translate Ramp’s AI applications and infrastructure into compelling solution narratives tied to measurable business outcomes.
Build ROI and total cost of ownership analyses that quantify the value of Ramp’s AI products and create executive-level justification for investment.
Help customers identify high-value use cases, set realistic expectations, and establish a credible path from evaluation to production.
Deliver tailored demonstrations, technical workshops, and proofs of concept with clear success criteria that establish value and build confidence in a purchase decision.
Build relationships with champions and decision-makers across Engineering, IT, Security, Finance, Operations, Procurement, and executive leadership.
Navigate questions related to APIs, integrations, model capabilities and limitations, data flows, architecture, privacy, security, governance, implementation, and tradeoffs among quality, cost, latency, and control.
Apply strong commercial judgment to qualify opportunities, create urgency, address objections, identify risk, and keep customers moving toward a decision.
Lead customers through implementation after purchase, including deployment planning, stakeholder alignment, workflow design, technical coordination, enablement, and adoption.
Partner with Account Executives and collaborate with Product, Engineering, Security, Marketing, and post-sales teams to remove deployment blockers and deliver a strong customer experience from evaluation through production.
Bring structured customer and market feedback to internal teams to improve the products, positioning, sales execution, and customer experience.
Turn early customer conversations into repeatable messaging, demonstrations, qualification criteria, value stories, and sales plays as we build this go-to-market motion from the ground up.

What you’ll bring

5+ years of experience in Solutions Engineering, Solutions Consulting, technical sales, Solutions Architecture, enterprise software sales, or a related customer-facing role.
Direct quota-carrying or deal-closing ownership of the pre-sale cycle—not only experience delivering demonstrations or supporting post-sale implementation.
A track record of independently influencing and winning complex B2B sales opportunities with clear revenue accountability.
Strong discovery and value-selling skills, with the ability to connect technical capabilities to measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to build executive-level business cases, including ROI and total cost of ownership analyses; this capability will be central to success in the role.
Commercial instincts and comfort taking meaningful ownership of deal strategy, momentum, and results.
Technical fluency across modern AI systems, including applications and agents, model capabilities and limitations, APIs, integrations, data flows, security, governance, and tradeoffs among quality, cost, latency, and control.
Excellent executive communication and presentation skills, including the ability to make complex concepts clear and relevant to different audiences.
The ability to explain probabilistic, rapidly evolving AI technology with credibility and precision without overpromising what the product can do.
Experience building champions and navigating multi-threaded buying groups with competing priorities.
High ownership, curiosity, sound judgment, and comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where you’ll build structure as you go rather than inherit it.
Energy for zero-to-one work and the opportunity to build a sales motion rather than simply inherit one.

Nice to have

Experience selling AI infrastructure, AI applications or agents, developer tools, data platforms, security products, finance technology, or workflow automation software.
Experience helping launch a new product or develop an early go-to-market motion.
Familiarity with AI gateways, model routing, usage controls, data governance, or enterprise AI deployment.
Experience selling to developers, IT, Security, Finance, Operations, Procurement, or executive stakeholders.
Experience creating reusable sales assets, demonstrations, value frameworks, or enablement programs.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Principal Data Scientist – Market Access
new_jobs.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Do you want to build agentic AI systems that reach real patients and inform real business decisions?

The Lilly USA Technology at Lilly Market Access team is seeking a Senior Principal Data Scientist to design and build the next generation of agentic AI and machine learning solutions across our employer-intelligence and real-world-evidence initiatives. You will work with internal business and Technology at Lilly partners to solve complex, high-volume problems with intelligent, autonomous, and measurable AI systems that scale horizontally across use cases.

What You'll Be Doing

As a Senior Principal Data Scientist, you will analyze complex data, develop predictive and generative models, and design agentic AI systems that solve genuine business problems in the employer and real-world-evidence spaces. You will own the AI reasoning layer end to end, from framing the problem and designing multi-agent workflows to building the models and evaluation frameworks that make these systems trustworthy. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to understand business problems, develop hypotheses, and test them with data and rigorous evaluation. You will build reusable, horizontal capabilities rather than one-off solutions.

How You'll Succeed

Design and build agentic AI systems, including agent-to-agent orchestration, multi-agent workflows, tool and environment use, and autonomous reasoning loops that act on real systems.
Build rigorous AI evaluation frameworks, including groundedness and hallucination measurement, benchmark design, regression testing, confidence and uncertainty estimation, and human-in-the-loop review, so AI behavior is measurable and defensible.
Apply ML fundamentals, including supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, natural language processing, time-series, and statistical inference, to the employer-signal and real-world-evidence domains.
Develop, fine-tune, and distill models, including small, specialized models trained on proprietary data, with appropriate governance and data controls.
Apply modern LLM techniques, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector search, and knowledge-graph methods, to ground AI reasoning in trusted, cited sources.
Design reusable, horizontal AI capabilities that can be surfaced across multiple downstream experiences and teams, rather than rebuilding logic for each use case.
Ensure data quality, reproducibility, and auditability across all models and agentic workflows, consistent with a regulated environment.
Translate business problems into solvable AI problems and communicate insights and recommendations to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Conduct research and stay current with the AI frontier, bringing emerging agentic, evaluation, and model-training techniques into the team's work.
Provide technical leadership, including setting the technical direction for agentic AI work, mentoring other team members, and defining evaluation and model-development standards for the team.
Manage and prioritize multiple projects simultaneously.

What You Should Bring

Foundational knowledge in communication, leadership, teamwork, problem solving, solution and blueprint definition, business acumen, architectural processes (e.g., blueprinting, reference architecture, governance), technical standards, project delivery, and the industry.

Business Analysis And Technical Leadership, Including

Engaging with the business and proactively seeking opportunities to deliver business value.
Understanding business requirements and effectively translating business needs and processes into technical terms, and vice versa.
Eliciting and defining requirements.
Ensuring appropriate business roles are engaged in solution execution.
Participating in design reviews to ensure traceability of requirements.
Networking with appropriate Technology at Lilly colleagues to determine solutions that meet business partners' needs.
Seeking opportunities to reuse existing processes and services to streamline support and implementation of key systems.
Staying abreast of tools and technologies to influence Technology at Lilly strategy so that it provides the best usage opportunities for the business.

Basic Qualifications

PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative or technical field, with at least 4 + years of experience developing, deploying, or maintaining AI, machine learning, or data systems in production environments.
OR Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative or technical field, with at least 6 + years of experience developing, deploying, or maintaining AI, machine learning, or data systems in production environments.
OR Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative or technical field, with at least 8 + years of experience developing, deploying, or maintaining AI, machine learning, or data systems in production environments.

Preferred Qualifications

A track record of delivering LLM or agentic AI solutions into production that produced measurable business results.
Strong foundation in machine learning algorithms and statistical analysis.
Proficiency in Python.
Proven experience providing technical leadership, such as setting the technical direction of AI or ML projects, mentoring data scientists or engineers, or defining standards for model development and evaluation.
Agentic AI: experience designing agent-to-agent orchestration and multi-agent workflows with modern agentic frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, LangChain, or equivalent), including tool use and autonomous reasoning loops.
AI evaluation: experience building evaluation and benchmarking approaches for LLM and agentic systems, including groundedness, hallucination, and reliability measurement, and integrating evaluation into the development lifecycle.
LLM techniques: experience with prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector databases, knowledge graphs, and fine-tuning or distillation of small, specialized models.
ML fundamentals: experience with supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, NLP, time-series, and uncertainty quantification.
Platforms and tooling: experience with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure, Databricks, SQL and NoSQL data stores, deep learning frameworks, common data-manipulation libraries, Git, and CI/CD.
Domain: previous experience in healthcare, pharma, payer or employer, or real-world evidence.
Demonstrated ability to analyze large, complex data domains, to craft practical, measurable AI solutions, and to communicate with a geographically dispersed group of business and technical colleagues.

About The Organization

Lilly IT builds and maintains capabilities with cutting-edge technologies, as the most prominent tech companies do. Lilly IT is different because we use technology to advance our purpose: creating medicines that make life better for people around the world. Examples include data-driven drug discovery, connected clinical trials, and AI that helps patients access and afford their medicines. We hire the best technology professionals from a variety of backgrounds so they can bring an assortment of knowledge, skills, and diverse thinking to deliver innovative solutions in every area of our business.

The Lilly USA Technology at Lilly team is at the forefront of leveraging data and technology to launch new medicines to market, raise awareness, and help appropriate patients get access to medication. We partner closely with Lilly's market access organization, which works with payers, employers, and government customers to improve affordability and broaden access. With a deep technical and business understanding, working across all therapeutic areas and disease states, we design and implement digital solutions to power our business. We use real-world evidence and health outcomes data to reduce friction across the patient journey, create best-in-class customer engagements, improve patient outcomes, and deliver business results.

0–10%

Please note this is for individuals to request an accommodation as part of the application process and any other correspondence will not receive a response.
